title: Structs, enums, and Result

spans.text: LESSON PURPOSE

Goal: apply “Structs, enums, and Result” to a real program or device. The key principle is: Result<T, E> encodes success and failure in the type. In a project, follow this guidance: Returning Result makes the caller's error-handling choice explicit.

CORE EXPLANATION

A struct groups related fields; an enum models alternatives. Result<T, E> represents success or failure explicitly; match and ? make error flow visible.

A struct groups related fields, while a tuple struct creates a distinct type without named fields. An enum is a finite set of variants, each optionally carrying data. `impl` attaches methods and associated functions; `match` destructures variants and checks exhaustiveness. `Option<T>` models absence and `Result<T,E>` models success or failure explicitly, replacing implicit null/error flows with typed alternatives.
